correctness.rationale: Each spanning tree has precisely one doubly attached vertex on the n-side; elementary square-cycle inspection gives the full 3(n-1)-regular exchange graph. The proposed distance admits a constructive optimal path and a rigorous unit-Lipschitz lower bound. A complete Walsh basis on the wildcard slices gives invariant matrices (n-3-2r)I+2J and hence every Laplacian eigenvalue and multiplicity. Distance spheres, Wiener index, and Kirchhoff product are exact consequences. One direct edge-subset enumerator and one separately implemented wildcard-state checker passed their stated finite ranges; finite tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The restricted one-edge fundamental square exchange is a natural local operation on spanning trees of K_{2,n}. This all-parameter result gives a sharp geodesic metric, a uniform distribution of shortest-path lengths, a constant spectral gap and an exact spanning-tree product for the reconfiguration graph. These nontrivial graph-invariant classifications are not deduced simply from the already-known enumeration of configurations and provide a concrete benchmark for constrained matroid exchange dynamics.
